close_reason: Added FileNodeBackend::query_subtree (default: O(depth) loop, backends can override with one query); updated handle_filenode_query to call query_subtree; updated MockBackend in tests/common; regression test added; 25 tests pass; clippy clean.
description:
The current FileNode/query depth implementation in handle_filenode_query calls query_objects with a parentId filter once per depth level (one backend call per level). Efficient backends (e.g. those with a nested-sets model or closure table) can answer a depth-N subtree query in a single operation, but there is no trait method for this.

Required addition:

1. Add to FileNodeBackend:

root_idsmax_depthmax_depth = 0max_depth = u64::MAXquery_objectsparentId

2. Update handle_filenode_query in filenode.rs to use query_subtree instead of the current depth-loop when depth > 0.

3. Update MockBackend in tests/common/mod.rs to implement query_subtree using the existing set_children map.

4. Add tests:
   - depth=1 via query_subtree returns same results as current loop
   - depth=2 returns grandchildren
   - max_depth=u64::MAX returns full subtree

Oracle: draft-ietf-jmap-filenode-13 §3.2.5 — depth is a query parameter; the spec does not constrain the implementation to N round-trips.

Acceptance criteria:
- FileNodeBackend::query_subtree has a working default impl (loop)
- handle_filenode_query uses query_subtree when depth > 0
- All existing depth tests still pass
- cargo test -p jmap-filenode-server exits 0
- Clippy clean
title: jmap-filenode-server: Add query_subtree to FileNodeBackend for O(1) depth queries
